paragraphs: R' Aivu bar Nagri, [Rosh Hashanah 21a](https://www.sefaria.org/Rosh_Hashanah.21a.4); Dikdukei Soferim reads bar Nagra.
R' Mashin bar Nagri; [Bereshit Rabbah 82:5](https://www.sefaria.org/Bereshit_Rabbah.82.5) (Hyman cites 82:4).[^1][^2]

notes.text: דק״ס is read contextually as Dikdukei Soferim; וגרסת introduces the attributed reading bar-Nagra and is not itself a variant word. No fresh collation is claimed.

The linked Bavli gives Aivu bar Nagri. [Heilprin’s Aivu entry](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=390&lang=en) cites this folio under Nagra, the form Hyman attributes to Dikdukei Soferim. In the linked Bereshit Rabbah, the digital witness has Mashin ben Nagri with Nagdi bracketed. [Heilprin’s Mashin entry](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=2455&lang=en) gives him as bar Nagri and names the same group of transmitters. The locators and patronymic forms differ.
